title: Rerun every check after any fix
statement: After any change or fix, re-run every check and quality measure on the whole set, passed items included, because a fix for one can break another.
example: A speaker-label fix passed a 1466/1466 live battery and still turned the full suite red.
detail: In the reading project, a speaker-label fix passed every targeted check, including a machine re-listen, walkers and a 1466/1466 live battery, and still turned the full check suite red, because a validator comparing the exact field it touched ran nowhere in the listening pipeline. Each targeted verifier reads one slice of the contract, so any edit to the course file now runs the full suite on the final tree before commit. Re-run after any change, not only a fix, with no check switched off, add a fresh balanced set, and look for new kinds of failure.
against: the rewrite pilot was small, and the project's own rule is not to report its four surviving items as the production result. The reports do not say what each update changed, so which change caused which effect is not known. The judge flips verdicts on identical generations ("The InceptBench evaluator has a **20% rating-flip rate** on identical generations across 4 repeated trials.", `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/CLAUDE.md`, line 101), so control regressions of 5.1% to 9.0% against a 3% limit may be judge noise rather than real regressions, and a limit set below the judge's noise reverts every change. The control samples were small (`--control-pct 15`, the same file, line 192). The source is a proposal and reports no result of this test (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0128-externalized-pedagogy-policy-compiler-decision.qmd`). The same change was a real gain on multiple choice (`project_richer_rag_per_cell_tradeoff.md`, line 19). The full-set run compared fresh outputs with a stored baseline, which by itself moved short answers by 3.60 points (`feedback_baseline_must_be_fresh_gen.md`, line 24), so part of the drop may be that artifact. the faults it names are in a course package's documents and counts, not in its items. The report doesn't say how many changes the run made, so it shows that a fix for one dimension can break others, not that making one change at a time avoids it. A later run found: a planned editor stage would re-check only a step a person edits by hand, not every check on the whole set (`g9/transformer/v03/README.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/WORKFLOW.md`).
